updates.predecessor_meaning: S.2503's complete Senate-passed ES was offered February23 and put to the recorded House suspension-and-passage vote February24. The motion FAILED264-133 under the two-thirds requirement despite majority Yea votes; neither this choice nor the earlier voice response establishes House passage or enactment. Section3 would immediately narrow91.225(f)(1)sensitive-government missions, excluding routine, non-classified, proficiency and below-Cabinet/Joint-Chiefs-Chair official flights, with ATC notice when not transmitting and monthly notice of ClassBmissions to named committees. The retained baseline exception already requires FAA authorization and specified defense/homeland-security/intelligence/law-enforcement operational-security/safety conditions; the separate ATC-direction exception is not the same branch. FAA must update regulations and agency agreements within one year, with status reporting if late. Agency attestations beginning within90days and quarterly thereafter/flight lists/classified annexes, FAA180day-then-biannual reports and special notices, a two-year GAO before/after review, FAA continuation determinations for noncompliant operators and annual DOT-IG audits beginning after three years provide distinct oversight, not proof of actual noncompliance. Section4 requires an ADS-B In final rule within two years, effective within60days of publication, with equipage by December31,2031 for aircraft required to have ADS-B Out, excluding unmanned aircraft and retaining ATC authorization. Alternative performance-compliant equipment is required for part91aircraft with maximum certificated takeoff weight below12,500pounds and qualifying military aircraft, with military briefing and other guidance; this is not an unconditional all-aircraft mandate. A qualified in-service operator may request up to one additional year, requiring an acceptable application/progress attestation, significant-disruption determination and no uncorrected specified violations; it is not a blanket extension. A negotiated-rulemaking committee is optional, with consultation required if absent; conditional committee/proposal duties, low-cost alternatives and proactive equipage apply as printed. The rulemaking includes a rebuttable cost-benefit/safety PRESUMPTION, not this candidate's empirical conclusion. Separation-standard proposed rulemaking, FAA order changes and controller training have separate relative clocks; an ACAS-X deployment action plan is mandatory while implementation actions are permissive. ARAC reviews ClassDequipment needs rather than automatically extending the mandate to all ClassDoperations. Section5repeals only FY2026NDAA373(a), applying chapter157as if its amendments had not been enacted; that removes the specified military training-flight proximity-warning limitation/waiver framework in covered DCairspace, not373(b)near-miss reports. Section6requires an Army-IG coordination/training/equipment/maintenance/incident audit initiated within60days, periodic progress briefings, unredacted congressional results and public results subject to national-security redaction. Section7establishes/designates an FAA-DOD coordination office within30days and requires the specified DCreview, risk-prioritized other-airport reviews, consultations, incident analyses and staffing. DC initiation is within30days after office establishment and completion within120days of review initiation; other ClassB/C/Dinitiation deadlines are sequential90day clocks and completion within180days of each initiation. DCresults go to Congress within60days of completion; other results are reported every six months after enactment. Section8requires safety-information-sharing MOUs with Army within60days and Navy/AirForce/CoastGuard within90days, with seven-day congressional notice. Section9DEEMS the May10,2024FAA-DODagreement to be the joint notice under FY2019section1046(b), making1046(a)cease as of that date under the proposal; it does not independently prove the historical notice was submitted. The agreement must be updated consistently with section3regulations and remains subject to joint modification, either Secretary's termination or law. Baseline1046(a)limited ADS-B installation/service/access requirements for fighter/bomber/special-mission aircraft until the specified joint notice. No actual equipment installation, regulation, MOU, appropriation, prevented accident, agency motive or safety outcome is inferred.

updates.predecessor_meaning: H.R.2189 is the complete two-title package deemed adopted under H.Res.1057 using RCP119-18, then put to final passage. TitleI adds a less-than-lethal projectile-device exception alongside the existing antique-firearm exception in18USC921(a)(3), and adds(39). A qualifying device must satisfy ALL conditions: it is not designed/intended to expel and cannot readily be converted to accept/discharge common handgun/rifle/shotgun ammunition OR any other projectile over500feet per second; is designed/intended for use not likely to cause death or serious bodily injury; and cannot accept or readily be modified to accept feeding devices loaded inside a pistol grip OR commonly used in semiautomatic firearms. A requested Attorney General determination is due90days after receipt of the DEVICE. These are classification criteria, not a finding that every labeled device is harmless or an exception limited to police purchasers. TitleII exempts qualifying devices, devices on the Secretary's separate above500feet-per-second list, and shells/cartridges satisfying the intended-use/injury criterion and designed for those devices, from4181 manufacturer/producer/importer sales excise tax. The ordinary device definition repeats the feature/design limits. A manufacturer/producer/importer classification request has a90day decision clock after receipt of the REQUEST; requests during the initial180days are deemed received at that period's close. The Secretary must publish and annually update both the ordinary qualifying-device list and the separate list that would qualify except for the500feet-per-second condition, with an annual congressional report explaining inclusion/exclusion from the latter. Section203 adds both device categories to5845(a)National Firearms Act definition exclusions. That separate listed-device tax/NFA route does NOT expand TitleI's921(a)(39)definition. The tax amendments apply to articles sold after enactment as printed. Existing military/small-manufacturer/paid-NFA excise exceptions, antique/qualified collector-device NFA exclusions, and119-21section70436's enacted transfer/making-tax and4182(a)changes remain context; no universal prior tax burden or first-ever federal device exemption is asserted. Existing INA237(a)(2)(C)expressly incorporates firearm OR destructive device as defined in921(a); its in-and-admitted chapeau, after-admission CONVICTION, specified conduct and violation-of-law conditions remain. TitleI does not amend921(a)(4)'s separate destructive-device definition, so an exception to the firearm branch does not establish immunity under every route or other law. Existing922(g)(5)firearm/ammunition restrictions distinguish unlawful presence and nonimmigrant-visa admission with retained(y)exceptions/waivers; not all noncitizens have the same predicate. No individual device/conviction classification, adjudication, retroactive immigration relief, State use-of-force change, actual sale/tax saving, enactment or safety effect is inferred. This is one whole-bill choice, not a component endorsement.

defective_s2503_preimage: Alternative performance-compliant equipment is required for part91aircraft with maximum certificated takeoff weight below12,500pounds and qualifying military aircraft, with military briefing and other guidance; this is not an unconditional all-aircraft mandate.
corrected_s2503_passage: FAA must establish performance requirements for an acceptable alternative-equipment pathway for part 91 aircraft with maximum certificated takeoff weight below 12,500 pounds and qualifying military aircraft specified in consultation with Defense. Eligible operators may use an FAA-acceptable alternative to satisfy the ADS-B In requirement; they are not required to choose alternative equipment. The printed situational-awareness, portable/display, avionics and airworthiness conditions and military briefing duties remain; this is not an unconditional all-aircraft mandate.
controlling_complete_clause: (B) Alternative equipment or technology.--With respect to aircraft with a maximum certificated takeoff weight of less than 12,500 pounds when operating under part 91 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations, and qualifying military aircraft as specified by the Administrator in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Administrator shall establish performance requirements for alternative equipment or technology that the Administrator determines acceptable in satisfying the ADS-B In requirement. The performance requirements shall, at a minimum-- (i) provide similar or improved situational awareness to the location of other airborne traffic, as well as traffic advisory information; and (ii) leverage the use of portable ADS-B In receivers or equipment that allow display on an existing or future electronic flight bag or panel mounted display, provided that the installation or use of such equipment does not adversely affect other required avionics or the airworthiness of the aircraft.
